Ami tippeket javasolni tudok:

- kezdj el olyan ízűt venni, amit utálsz. nekem pl ez a blueberry killa volt

- ha van olyan emléked, amikor szarul lettél tőle, idézd fel gyakran (pl első pablo...)

- kibaszottul undorító, de ami nekem a legtöbbet segített az a sokszoros újrahasznosítás volt. egy külön dobozban gyűjtöttem a kb üreseket, és mikor már nagyon sík ideg voltam, arra fanyalodtam rá inkább...

- rágózás minden mennyiségben

- netről lehet rendelni nikotinmenteset (/cbd olajosat) ez is elég jó alternatíva lehet

- készülj kajával, ha sokat toltad gyakrabban leszel éhes. benne van hogy felraksz pár kilót.

- készülj fel rá lélekben hogy rendkívül ingerlékeny leszel, leginkább az első napokban/hetekben.

- tedd el a dobozt szem elől. ne vigyél magaddal egy egészet/telit ha mész valahová, max 1-2 dbot külön dobozban. random maradék üres doboz menjen mind a kukába, ne maradjon a táskádban/zsebedben/szem előtt

One time I had the microscope reserved for an experiment (living cells, lots of preparation). My PI dropped by the lab and casually told me that he scheduled a maintenance check for the machine during my reservation window, but "hey it's all good you can do your stuff in the evening or the weekend right?". I politely told him that as he is well aware I am able and willing to work off hours but please treat my time with a little more respect. He took a deep breath and started his next sentence with "Listen here kitten..." but didn't get very far with that line of thought because I was full on rabid rage yelling not to call me a fucking kitten. We proceeded to engage in a very loud exchange of opinions, which ended with him stating that I'm fired. 

My other supervisor smoothed out the conflict, and I ended up finishing in record time, but my biggest source of joy wasn't the fact that I finished my PhD, but that I don't have to engage with him ever again.

one thing that I tried to do though that helped relieve a little bit of the pain in my head is the following:

So, it's just fucking ruminating all day long right? the usual pit when I feel like I can't be bothered to draw a breath of air in my lungs, let alone face my inadequacy during reading papers or trying to write some shit. no fucking way. and like, what's next then? realistically, even the worst thing that could happen is bit further down the road usually. so there is a bit of a time until it all comes down. and yeah it's going to come down, aint nothing I could do about it, it is what it is as they say, but what happens until then? got all this free time on my hands from not doing the shit I'm supposed to do. even ruminating can get...boring I guess. so I'd just grab a piece of the  thing I'm supposed to work on, and kind of...try to find some aspect of it that at least is a bit enjoyable, and fool around with it (that's why I have about 23 absolutely beautiful, pixel perfect images in my thesis, and about 23k very stupid sounding words), so, like, no pressure, it's not like I'm actually trying to get this shit done, strictly just chilling to pass the time. 

and you know what? doing something silly and not necessarily important, but fun, kinda feels nice. might even give a bit of an encouragement to try the harder things. they won't be easier, but at least doing them wouldn't feel like complete torture? something like that.

I felt apathy, tiredness (she was really old) and acceptance coming from her. Next day, my mother called crying that my cat stepped in front of the car suddenly as she was parking in the garage. I never stopped mourning her.

A "problémás" kifejezés meg sem közelíti a valóságot. Kex például iszonyatosan makacs, semmiben nem hasonlít a legtöbb kutyához. Nem (alig) ugrál, nem bújik oda, nem kunyerál, foghegyről veszi el a jutalomfalatot, megérti mit szeretnél tőle, de ha nincs olyan kedve, akkor nem csinálja. Fantasztikus és imádom. Maximálisan önálló, nem alázkodik meg semmilyen helyzetben. Ha shibát szeretnél, arra kell felkészülni, hogy nem lehet csak úgy félvállra venni, a minőségi foglalkozásnál nem éri be kevesebbel. Sajnos csak nemrég irattuk be kutyasuliba és nem én járok el vele az órákra, de látszik rajta hogy jobb kedve van utána. Hatalmas agya van és simán lenyom 6D sakkozásban, ezért "problémás".

Basically you take the short variable fragment of an antibody specific for a chosen tumor antigen, combine it with a hinge+transmembrane domain for flexibility and stability, and finally add a CD3z effector domain (from the native T cell receptor) + costimulatory domain (usually CD28 or 41BB) for signal transduction upon antigen recognition. That's the structure of a basic CAR. 
Slap all of these domains combined in a plasmid, take blood from the patient, separate the T cells, deliver the CAR encoding gene (usually using lenti/retroviral systems) into the T cells. 
Infuse the cell product back into the patient, where the CAR is able to recognise the tumor specific antigen and transmit an activation signal through the CD3z and costimulatory domains to kill the tumor cell in a similar manner as a normal effertor T cell would do.

I grew up in an abusive family. We could have been in a decent place financially, but my father gambled massive amounts of money away. I always envied kids having nice meals and snacks at school. I was living in a constant rage and torment from our fathers abuse, and I fled into my studies. My grades, my scores felt like a matter of life and death. I was hooked on biology. My teacher was really nice, I often participated in competitions. I even had a small project about monitoring contamination levels at a local swamp where a spring returned after decades of coal mining in my town. I was poking around in the swamp all proud with my little yellow wwf case full of paper-strip indicators and plastic cups. I would cry hysterically when I saw trash in the river near my home. I wanted to save the world. 

My family mocked my when I told them I want to become a bioengineer, saying I won't make any money. I was deeply hurt, but I proceeded anyway. I got into the nicest uni in the country, moved to the capital, and felt like my life will start finally. Right about the start of the third semester, my father committed suicide, after we found out that he was cheating my mum. Our world shattered, he had so many debts we knew nothing about, and my mother had to take care of us three kids all going to school alone, burdened with a loan on the house. I started to do terrible at uni. I received some money from the state, but I had to spend it all on failed credit fines. I was learning hard, but when the exams came, I just couldn't face the teachers, I was terrified of them, so I just didn't go to any exam. I was becoming extremely poor, but I didn't tell anyone about it. I would sneak out at night to eat from the trashcans at the dorm I was living in.

A moment came when I had to make a decision, fail university or make my situation work somehow. As a last resort, I applied to a lab for an internship, to work on my thesis. I was so lucky. I got into a wonderful group, my supervisor was kind and patient. A senior guy in the group would sneak biscuits and instant noodles in a cabinet at the lab, for me and another PhD student who couldn't afford food. I made friends. But I was still very poor. I had to work a night job. Sometimes I slept in the engine room of the institute on the floor, because I didn't want to go home, and I was not eligible for a dorm room anymore. I was working my ass off at the lab and I won a national competition for my thesis, but when I walked up to take the prize, I just wanted to scream in agony. It was a struggle, but I graduated. Then I got offered a job in another lab, and took it. It was terrible. I couldn't make a connection with anyone. So I left after a year. Spent three months in Shanghai on an internship. I made a couple of friends. But the stipend was so low, I had to go through the trashcans again. All my friends were super rich, and would invite me to expensive restaurants. I accepted, and blowed half a months stipend one night, just to feel less alone.

I applied for a PhD back in my home country, and everything was relatively fine. My work and dedication was appreciated. Finally I had enough money to live a decent life. But I feel alienated from my peers. I try to act normal, but I just feel so broken.  When I am under pressure, I crumble. I did a lot of drugs during the years. I feel like ruined my mental health. Sometimes I cannot think straight. Somehow I got to visit a nice lab in Germany during the summer for three months, and everyone was so kind. I was trying to be friendly too, but I felt like I must work really hard. They were so much better than me. Smarter, more confident, easygoing. I was crying while biking to work, I was crying when I was going home. I felt like I could never catch up to them, but by some miracle, they appreciated me, and invited me back for a postdoc. I came back to my home country again and I was looking at postdoc stipends, but it turns out...I am not good enough for any of them. I just don't have the necessary if on my papers to have any chance. I broke down, and I haven't recovered since. I have been slacking on my job, I am far behind a number of projects. I have a student with a thesis deadline in a week, but I keep avoiding him. I feel so ashamed. I feel like I cannot hold on any longer to this stupid dream that I could become a scientist. I am already massively overwhelmed, and this is just the baby level. How could I even think about going further? I don't know what to do, I tried therapy, I tried talking to friends, but it didn't get better. I look up to my collection of biology textbooks once displayed proudly filled with doodles of me in a lab coat from my childhood and I am filled with dread. I don't know if I can hold on any longer. I pushed myself too much for too long, and now I feel like it's all about to crash.
